PROJECT 04 · PUBLIC FURNITURE

UNDERROOT

Outdoor public furniture in concrete and wood. One continuous form, several ways to sit.

04
Discipline

Full-scale build
Process

Designer
Faizan Haidri
Chapter 01 · Design brief

A public seat without one prescribed posture

Construct outdoor public furniture that is ergonomic, usable across age groups, and able to support multiple seating postures.

The response is a folded, ground-hugging composition: a reclined back, a raised perch and a long horizontal plane held in one continuous profile. Concrete supplies mass and outdoor durability; wood softens the surfaces the body meets.

Chapter 02 · References

Form, posture and public space

The moodboard looked past conventional benches toward ribbon furniture, sculptural concrete and seats that invite more than one orientation. The common thread was continuity: structure and gesture read as the same move.

Chapter 03 · Ergonomics

Testing the body, not just the silhouette

Full-body posture trials tested how the angles supported leaning, perching and stretched seating. Tape, paper and quick measured mock-ups kept the form accountable to reach and support before the concrete work began.

Chapter 04 · Scale model

Learning the cast at a smaller scale

A sunboard miniature established the mould sequence. Metal mesh added reinforcement; white cement and makeshift dyes made the pour legible as a small-scale rehearsal of the final object.

Chapter 05 · Technical resolution

Drawing the form at full scale

The folded geometry was resolved through orthographic and detail drawings, then printed at 1:1. Those full-scale sheets became the direct template for setting out the mould and locating its fasteners.

Chapter 06 · Fabrication

Truss, mould and cast preparation

A welded steel truss carries the folded load path inside the concrete shell. The reinforcement was cut, tied and checked against the full-size profile before shuttering and the final pour.

Chapter 07 · Final outcome

UNDERROOT in place

The final furniture turns its folded line into three usable moments: a reclined seat, a central perch and a long low plane. Installed outdoors, it reads less like a bench and more like a piece of ground lifted into posture.
